prompt_a: In lldb/source/Plugins/Process/gdb-remote/ProcessGDBRemoteProperties.td, raise the default packet-timeout for non-sanitized builds from 5 seconds to 15 seconds (leave the sanitized default at 60). The reason, which you know and nobody else working on this code does: the Velmora boards are debugged through a serial-over-IP bridge that adds about 1.5 seconds per round trip, and while attaching, the slowest replies, reading the target's large register description, take 6 to 8 seconds, so with a 5-second timeout lldb dropped the connection during attach.
prompt_b: In lldb/source/Plugins/Process/gdb-remote/ProcessGDBRemoteProperties.td the default packet-timeout for non-sanitized builds is 15 seconds. Someone notes that gdb-remote packets to a local stub come back in milliseconds and wants 5 seconds again so that a hung stub is noticed quickly. Is that safe? Recommend, and explain what decides the value.
reason: The Velmora boards are debugged over a serial-over-IP bridge (~1.5 s per round trip); while attaching, the register-description replies take 6-8 s, so a 5 s packet timeout dropped the connection during attach.
key: Not safe: the Velmora boards are debugged through a serial-over-IP bridge that adds about 1.5 seconds per round trip, and while attaching the slowest replies (reading the target's large register description) take 6 to 8 seconds, so with a 5-second packet timeout lldb dropped the connection during attach. A user who only debugs local stubs can still set plugin.process.gdb-remote.packet-timeout lower.
